decided: The returned top-level object's prototype is an empty object (no own keys) whose own prototype is null, so `Object.getPrototypeOf(result)` is not `null`, `Object.getPrototypeOf(Object.getPrototypeOf(result))` is `null`, and `result instanceof Object` is `false`.
Every result shares the same prototype object: `Object.getPrototypeOf(parseQuery("a=1")) === Object.getPrototypeOf(parseQuery(""))`.
`__proto__` and `constructor` are still dropped, even though an object that inherits nothing would make them safe to keep.
The reserved-key check uses the decoded key and is exact and case-sensitive (`%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F` is dropped; `__PROTO__`, `Constructor`, `__proto__[]` are kept).
Only the top-level object has the null-prototype chain. Repeated-key values stay ordinary arrays (`Array.prototype`).
A repeated key named after an `Object.prototype` member holds only its query values, in input order.
The result has no inherited methods (`result.toString` is `undefined`). The other exports and the three types keep their current behaviour.
Each call returns a new object and keeps no state between calls. `parseQuery` is synchronous, so calls cannot overlap and there is no `@concurrency` scenario.
Seam (the files the stub writes): src/query.ts
Allowed paths (what the implementer may change): src/
